feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: A judge blocks the government's tree-clearing spree at a municipal D.C. golf course
entry.summary: Locals and preservationists have long opposed Trump's plan to redevelop a municipal D.C. golf course. That legal fight escalated after the government cleared hundreds of trees on short notice.

entry.title: Cornell University bans frat parties, vows to address 'disturbing' campus culture
entry.summary: In a letter, Cornell's president apologized for what happened to the student who alleges she was raped by several men at a fraternity house in 2024 and promised 'meaningful action.'

entry.title: The Trump administration warns Ukraine it could cut off intel, Zelenskyy tells NPR
entry.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sat down for an interview with NPR at a time of renewed tensions with the White House.

entry.title: Writer Yiyun Li lost both of her sons. When words fell short, she turned to music
entry.summary: Li won a Pulitzer for her memoir about the suicides of her two sons. In her new novel, Music Against the Night, she writes about two young prodigies in the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

entry.title: What ice cream has to do with this year's Nobel Prize in economics
entry.summary: Prices can get sticky. That helps explain why recessions hurt so much — and what policymakers can do about them.

entry.title: Polls are a snapshot, and other helpful things to remember during the midterm elections
entry.summary: With Election Day just a few weeks away — and millions of votes already cast — midterm polls are everywhere. While polling can be a helpful tool to understand the electorate, it's not a crystal ball.

entry.title: Win or lose, independent candidates want to meet voters in the middle
entry.summary: Nearly 200 independent candidates in more than 100 congressional races are trying to prove there's an alternative to the two party system — even though the chance of winning is very low.

entry.title: Voters here will decide whether to force cities to build cheaper, smaller homes
entry.summary: Voters in Massachusetts will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. A growing number of states are doing the same to help ease a housing shortage.

entry.title: Some of the most pristine coral reefs have a secret weapon: birds
entry.summary: Coral reefs are facing increasing threats around the globe. But on a remote Pacific island, scientists have found that reefs can get help from a surprising ally: seabirds.
